pcs.pc_description: use cadastral maps as base to locate and identify the site for sampling and preparing fertility map

modules.module_title: Collect soil sample from the site

pcs.pc_description: explain the importance of soil testing to the farmers
communicate effectively with farmers to collect the soil sample
use khurpi, spade, tube auger, screw auger and other equipment necessary for taking the sample from appropriate place of right quality in right quantity
plan for one representative sample from one uniform area w.r.t. uniformity in slope, drainage, colour and past management practices
ensure sample is not collected directly after any cultural activity in the field

ensure sample is not collected from unusual area like unevenly fertilized, marshy, old path, old channel, area near the tree, site of previous compost piles and manure heaps , dead furrows, areas near main bunds or old bund, & irrigation channels other unrepresentative sites
ensure sample is not collected at the periphery or in a straight line
use various sampling techniques like random sampling, grid sampling, zone sampling accordingly
undertake sampling at several locations in a zig-zag pattern
remove the surface litter from the sampling spot
collect a uniform slice digging a V-shaped cut upto sampling depth depending on the type of crop
collect 4-5 slices in a plastic tray to get a definitive soil sample from the field
mix the sub-samples thouroughly and remove foreign materials like roots, stones, pebbles & gravel
dry the soil samples in open air and avoid contamination
reduce the bulk to about half to one kilogram by quartering or compartmentalization
avoid any type of contamination at all stages

modules.module_title: Pack, label and dispatch the soil and water samples to the lab for testing

pcs.pc_description: collect the samples in clean polythene bags (soil) or plastic bottles (water)
prevent the samples from getting contaminated with chemicals, fertilizers or manures
seal the sample bags & bottles immediately after collection
keep the sample bags & bottles in a cloth bag with proper labels

pcs.pc_description: receive the samples in the Sample Receiving Cell by checking the availability of required information

transfer the samples for analysis detailing the tests required, expected date of reporting, etc.
mix the soil sample homogeneously and leave it to attain equilibrium in the trays
dry the soil sample in open air to maintain natural environment
crush and grind the clods gently with the help of wooden pestle & mortar
remove all the gravel, limestone, stones, etc., from the sample and record their data separately
sieve the soil using recommended size mesh stainless steel sieves
place sufficient quantity of sieved soil sample in plastic bag appropriately labelled with permanent ink marker
discard the plant residues, gravel and other materials retained on the sieve

modules.module_title: Handle and store water samples for analysis

pcs.pc_description: store the water samples in glass bottles, previously sterilized or free from any contamination
refrigerate the water samples as soon as possible (do not allow to freeze)
label the water sample bottles with waterproof marker and seal them tightly to avoid any contamination/leakage
ensure shorter time period between collection and analysis for more reliable results

modules.module_title: Prepare manure/compost and plant samples for analysis

pcs.pc_description: collect and seal the manure/plant samples in polyethylene bags
store the manure/plant samples in freezer
clean and take fresh weight of the samples
dry the samples in hot air oven at recommended temperature & time and then weigh the sample
calculate percent(%) of dry matter in sample
grind the sample to fine size (20 mm. mesh sieve) and make it ready for NPK analysis
grind the sample more finely in porcelain mortar to avoid any metallic contamination for micro-nutrient analysis.
seal and label the samples in polyethylene bags and store in cool & dry place for analysis
keep the samples decontaminated from any outside material
